Subject: Post-demo: deployment route & urgent capacity request (Hosted -> Dedicated/VPC)

Hi Tom / Aisha —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and the follow-ups I promised:

1) What we heard on the call
- Primary need: bursty, high-concurrency payment normalization workloads (spikes at end-of-day and settlement windows).
- Current pain: intermittent throttling on your hosted setup leading to delayed settlements and customer-facing errors.
- Controls: requirement for strict data residency in us-east, and an upcoming internal audit that may require evidence of isolated infrastructure for PII.

2) Deployment options to consider (brief):
- Hosted API: fastest to get running, automatic scaling, lower upfront cost. Good if bursts are moderate and you can absorb transient throttling via retry/backoff.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and isolation; best when you need guaranteed tail latency and capacity during peak windows.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): for strong isolation and data controls (KMS integration, customer-managed networking) — longer setup and contract lead time.

Based on what you described, Dedicated capacity looks like the right tradeoff for the near-term: it addresses the immediate throttle incidents, gives you capacity predictability for settlement peaks, and supports the compliance ask. If the audit requires customer-managed networking, we can map a path from Dedicated -> VPC in a phased approach.

Action items I want to confirm:
- Can you share peak RPS and 95/99th latency targets (approx daily and peak-window)? (Aisha/Tom)
- Are there contractual constraints (procurement lead times, PII handling rules) that force a Private/VPC-only outcome? (procurement@payflux.com)
- Would you like us to spin a short Dedicated trial (48–72 hour reserved capacity window) to validate tail-latency and give you a mitigation while your audit runs? That is something we can prioritize this week.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_onepager.pdf, a draft mutual action plan (payflux_mutual_action_plan.xlsx) — both attached for your review.

If this aligns, I can loop in Lauren (ops approvals) and Marissa (SE) to scope sizing and procurement steps.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
